title: Unfair trade practices, discipline, fraud and privacy
summary: Michigan's banned trade practices, the $50 gift rule, fiduciary duties, license discipline and fines, insurance fraud penalties, and privacy notices.
objectives: Tell twisting, rebating and misrepresentation apart, plus other unfair practices
Apply the $50 gift limit, rebating penalties and fiduciary rules for premiums
Recall discipline tiers, fines, and fraud penalties and reporting immunity
Use PAPER to remember Michigan's privacy notice rules

scenes.title: Unfair trade practices, discipline, fraud and privacy
scenes.subtitle: What Michigan bans, what discipline and fines follow, insurance fraud, and privacy notices

beats.text: What you must never do as a producer, and what follows when someone does: discipline, fines, fraud penalties and privacy rules.
beats.say: What you must never do as a producer, and what follows when someone does: discipline, fines, fraud penalties and privacy rules.

scenes.title: Twisting, rebating, misrepresentation

columns.name: Twisting
points: Misleading or incomplete comparison of policies
Goal: get a policy dropped or replaced

columns.name: Rebating
points: Or any value not specified in the policy

columns.name: Misrepresentation
points: Misstating a policy's terms or benefits
Or misstating an insurer's financial condition

scenes.tell: What is the agent after? A switch is twisting; a payback is rebating; a false picture is misrepresentation.

beats.text: Three practices get mixed up. Twisting: a knowingly misleading representation or incomplete comparison of policies, to get a policy dropped or replaced.
beats.say: Three practices get mixed up. Twisting: a knowingly misleading representation or incomplete comparison of policies, to get a policy dropped or replaced.

beats.text: Rebating: giving back part of the premium or commission, or any valuable inducement not specified in the policy.
beats.say: Rebating: giving back part of the premium or commission, or any valuable inducement not specified in the policy.

beats.text: Misrepresentation: misstating a policy's terms or benefits, or an insurer's financial condition.
beats.say: Misrepresentation: misstating a policy's terms or benefits, or an insurer's financial condition.

beats.text: Ask what the agent is after: a switch is twisting, a payback is rebating, a false picture is misrepresentation.
beats.say: Ask what the agent is after: a switch is twisting, a payback is rebating, a false picture is misrepresentation.

items.label: Defamation
items.detail: False or malicious statements about an insurance business's finances, meant to injure

items.label: Boycott, coercion, intimidation
items.detail: Concerted acts that unreasonably restrain the business of insurance

items.label: Lender coercion
items.detail: No loan conditioned on buying through a particular agent or insurer

items.label: False advertising
items.detail: Untrue, deceptive or misleading, in any medium

items.label: Unfair discrimination
items.detail: No refusing someone solely because another insurer denied coverage

beats.text: Defamation: a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurance business's financial condition, meant to injure it.
beats.say: Defamation: a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurance business's financial condition, meant to injure it.

beats.text: Boycott, coercion or intimidation: concerted acts that unreasonably restrain the business of insurance.
beats.say: Boycott, coercion or intimidation: concerted acts that unreasonably restrain the business of insurance.

beats.text: A lender can't make a loan depend on buying insurance through a particular agent or insurer.
beats.say: A lender can't make a loan depend on buying insurance through a particular agent or insurer.

beats.text: Advertising can't be untrue, deceptive or misleading.
beats.say: Advertising can't be untrue, deceptive or misleading.

beats.text: And an insurer can't refuse you solely because another insurer denied you coverage.
beats.say: And an insurer can't refuse you solely because another insurer denied you coverage.

scenes.q: An agent offers to send a prospect $200 of his commission if she buys a homeowners policy. This is:
scenes.why: Returning part of the commission is a rebate: valuable consideration not specified in the policy.

beats.text: Which practice? An agent offers a prospect $200 of his commission if she buys a homeowners policy. Pick an answer.
beats.say: Which practice? An agent offers a prospect two hundred dollars of his commission if she buys a homeowners policy. Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Rebating: handing back commission is a payback, not a switch or a false statement.
reveal.say: Rebating: handing back commission is a payback, not a switch or a false statement.

scenes.title: Rebating and the $50 gift
scenes.hook: A Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at $50 a year.
items: P&C gift: merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year
Agent who rebates: license revoked; no new license for 1 year
Also a misdemeanor: fine up to $100 per violation
Insured who knowingly accepts: coverage reduced in proportion, plus fine up to $100

beats.text: A Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at $50 a year.
beats.say: A Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at fifty dollars a year.

beats.text: That means merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year. Older materials may show another figure; $50 is the 2018 amendment.
beats.say: That means merchandise costing the insurer fifty dollars or less per calendar year. Older materials may show another figure; fifty dollars is the twenty eighteen amendment.

beats.text: A rebating agent loses the license, with no new one for 1 year, plus a misdemeanor fine of up to $100 per violation.
beats.say: A rebating agent loses the license, with no new one for one year, plus a misdemeanor fine of up to one hundred dollars per violation.

beats.text: An insured who knowingly accepts a rebate has coverage reduced in proportion, plus a fine of up to $100.
beats.say: An insured who knowingly accepts a rebate has coverage reduced in proportion, plus a fine of up to one hundred dollars.

items.label: Segregate; never commingle
items.detail: Your own money only to open the account and to pay or avoid bank charges

items.label: Holding a return premium
items.detail: For future premiums only with the insured's written authorization

items.label: Late turnover
items.detail: Prima facie evidence of a fiduciary violation

beats.text: Premiums are fiduciary money: segregate them, never commingle. Add your own money only to open the account and to pay or avoid bank charges.
beats.say: Premiums are fiduciary money: segregate them, never commingle. Add your own money only to open the account and to pay or avoid bank charges.

beats.text: The account must be at a federally insured institution, and it may earn interest.
beats.say: The account must be at a federally insured institution, and it may earn interest.

beats.text: You may hold a return premium there for future premiums only with the insured's written authorization.
beats.say: You may hold a return premium there for future premiums only with the insured's written authorization.

beats.text: Late turnover of that money is prima facie evidence of a violation.
beats.say: Late turnover of that money is prima facie evidence of a violation.

scenes.title: License discipline: shall not issue vs may refuse

columns.name: Shall not issue
points: Violent, sexual or financial felony, any date
Forging a name on an insurance document
Knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person

columns.name: May refuse
points: License denied, suspended or revoked elsewhere
Using notes during the licensing exam

scenes.tell: Any of these can also bring probation, suspension, revocation or a fine for a current licensee.

beats.text: Now discipline, in two tiers. Shall not issue: a felony conviction within 10 years before applying, or a violent, sexual or financial felony at any time.
beats.say: Now discipline, in two tiers. Shall not issue: a felony conviction within ten years before applying, or a violent, sexual or financial felony at any time.

beats.text: Also forging someone's name on an insurance document, or knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person.
beats.say: Also forging someone's name on an insurance document, or knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person.

beats.text: May refuse: false or incomplete application information, other felonies, a license action in another state, or using notes during the exam.
beats.say: May refuse: false or incomplete application information, other felonies, a license action in another state, or using notes during the exam.

beats.text: Any of these can also cost a current licensee: probation, suspension, revocation or a fine.
beats.say: Any of these can also cost a current licensee: probation, suspension, revocation or a fine.

scenes.title: Maximum fines after a hearing
items: Didn't know
$1,000 each; $50,000 cap per order
Knew or should have known
$5,000 each; $50,000 cap per order
$5,000 each; $50,000 per 6 months
Violating the cease and desist order
Knowingly: $20,000 each; $100,000 cap

beats.text: After a hearing, the director issues a cease and desist order and may fine up to $1,000 per violation if you didn't know,
beats.say: After a hearing, the director issues a cease and desist order and may fine up to one thousand dollars per violation if you didn't know,

beats.text: or up to $5,000 if you knew or reasonably should have known.
beats.say: or up to five thousand dollars if you knew or reasonably should have known.

beats.text: Caps: $50,000 per licensing order. For trade practices, $10,000 total, or $50,000 per 6 months if you knew or should have.
beats.say: Caps: fifty thousand dollars per licensing order. For trade practices, ten thousand dollars total, or fifty thousand dollars per six months if you knew or should have.

beats.text: Breaking the order itself, knowingly for a licensing order: up to $20,000 per violation.
beats.say: Breaking the order itself, knowingly for a licensing order: up to twenty thousand dollars per violation.

scenes.title: Insurance fraud penalties
scenes.hook: Solo 4, Squad 10: committing fraud risks 4 years; plotting it with a partner risks 10. Either way, up to $50,000 and you pay it back.
items: Fraudulent act: done knowingly, with intent to injure, defraud or deceive
Solo 4: felony, up to 4 years and/or $50,000, plus restitution
Squad 10: agreement or conspiracy, up to 10 years and/or $50,000, plus restitution
Runner, capper or steerer: paid by a practitioner to bring in clients for claims

beats.text: Fraud next. A fraudulent insurance act is done knowingly, with intent to injure, defraud or deceive, like false material information on an application or claim.
beats.say: Fraud next. A fraudulent insurance act is done knowingly, with intent to injure, defraud or deceive, like false material information on an application or claim.

beats.text: Solo 4: a felony, up to 4 years, a fine up to $50,000, or both, plus restitution.
beats.say: Solo four: a felony, up to four years, a fine up to fifty thousand dollars, or both, plus restitution.

beats.text: Squad 10: agreeing or conspiring to commit one, up to 10 years, same fine cap.
beats.say: Squad ten: agreeing or conspiring to commit one, up to ten years, same fine cap.

beats.text: And a runner, capper or steerer is someone a practitioner pays to bring in clients or patients for claims.
beats.say: And a runner, capper or steerer is someone a practitioner pays to bring in clients or patients for claims.

scenes.title: Reporting suspected fraud
scenes.story: Tom, an agent in Lansing, thinks a client's repair estimate looks altered. In good faith, he reports it to the state police. The estimate turns out to be genuine, and the client sues Tom for slander.

items.label: An estimate is a statement
items.detail: Fraud-law statements include estimates, invoices, bills and claim forms

items.label: State police: an authorized agency
items.detail: So are local police, prosecutors and DIFS

items.label: No malice, not known to be false
items.detail: The reporter isn't liable for libel, slander or other torts

scenes.answer: Tom isn't liable for slander: he reported without malice and didn't know the information was false.

beats.text: Tom, a Lansing agent, reports a repair estimate he believes is altered to the state police, in good faith. It's genuine, and the client sues for slander. Is Tom liable?
beats.say: Tom, a Lansing agent, reports a repair estimate he believes is altered to the state police, in good faith. It's genuine, and the client sues for slander. Is Tom liable?

beats.text: An estimate counts as a statement under the fraud law, and the state police are an authorized agency.
beats.say: An estimate counts as a statement under the fraud law, and the state police are an authorized agency.

beats.text: Someone who reports suspected fraud without malice isn't liable for libel, slander or other torts, unless he knows the information is false.
beats.say: Someone who reports suspected fraud without malice isn't liable for libel, slander or other torts, unless he knows the information is false.

beats.text: So Tom isn't liable for slander.
beats.say: So Tom isn't liable for slander.

scenes.title: Privacy notices
scenes.hook: Think PAPER for privacy notices: Personal, At the start, Periodic, Exit, Real copy.
items: Personal: personal, family or household insurance, not business buyers
At the start, then Periodic: at least once in any 12 consecutive months
Exit: an opt-out window of 30 days from mailing is reasonable
Real copy: in writing, or electronic if agreed; never solely oral

beats.text: Privacy: think PAPER. Personal: the law covers personal, family or household insurance, not business buyers.
beats.say: Privacy: think PAPER. Personal: the law covers personal, family or household insurance, not business buyers.

beats.text: At the start: a notice no later than when the customer relationship begins. Periodic: at least once in any 12 consecutive months.
beats.say: At the start: a notice no later than when the customer relationship begins. Periodic: at least once in any twelve consecutive months.

beats.text: Exit: before sharing with a nonaffiliated third party, you generally must offer an opt-out. Allowing 30 days from mailing is reasonable.
beats.say: Exit: before sharing with a nonaffiliated third party, you generally must offer an opt-out. Allowing thirty days from mailing is reasonable.

beats.text: Real copy: in writing, or electronically if the consumer agrees. Never solely oral, and an office sign doesn't count.
beats.say: Real copy: in writing, or electronically if the consumer agrees. Never solely oral, and an office sign doesn't count.

scenes.q: Which is NOT an acceptable way to deliver a required privacy notice?
choices: Mailing a printed copy to the consumer
Posting it on a sign in your office lobby
Posting it online for an online customer who must acknowledge receipt
scenes.why: Notices go in writing, or electronically if the consumer agrees: by hand, by mail, or on a website with required acknowledgment. An office sign doesn't count.

beats.text: Which is NOT an acceptable way to deliver a privacy notice? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Which is not an acceptable way to deliver a privacy notice? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The office sign. A sign or general advertising doesn't count. Mail, hand delivery, or a website notice the online customer must acknowledge all work.
reveal.say: The office sign. A sign or general advertising doesn't count. Mail, hand delivery, or a website notice the online customer must acknowledge all work.

scenes.title: Recap
items: Twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates
P&C gift limit: $50 per calendar year, cost to the insurer
Premiums are fiduciary money: segregate, never commingle
Fraud: 4 years alone, 10 for a conspiracy; up to $50,000
Privacy: PAPER; 30-day opt-out window; never solely oral

beats.text: Recap: twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates. P&C gifts stay at $50 a year. Premiums are fiduciary money.
beats.say: Recap: twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates. P and C gifts stay at fifty dollars a year. Premiums are fiduciary money.

beats.text: Fraud is 4 years alone, 10 with a partner. And for privacy, think PAPER.
beats.say: Fraud is four years alone, ten with a partner. And for privacy, think PAPER.
